data.title: Railway Track Diverters
data.statement:
An automated rail yard contains [[N]] switches, numbered {{1}} to [[N]]. Each switch is initially set to {{L}} (Left) or {{R}} (Right) and has a target for each direction. A target is either another switch, or a terminal depot with an identifier that is not a switch number.

• All trains are dispatched sequentially.
• Each train starts at switch {{1}}.
• When a train enters a switch, it follows the target indicated by the switch's current direction, then the switch toggles to the opposite direction.
• The new direction applies to the subsequent train that enters the switch.
• A train stops when it reaches a terminal depot.

Given the initial switch states and track layout, determine the terminal depot reached by each train.

STATEMENT
Simulate trains navigating track diverter switches that toggle state on pass.

INPUT
n: number of switches
t: number of trains dispatched
id: switch number
initialState: starting direction L or R
leftTarget: next target when L
rightTarget: next target when R

OUTPUT
exitDepot: depot reached by each train
data.inputDescription:

<<Line 2>>: An integer [[T]] representing the number of trains to dispatch.

• [[id]]: switch number
• [[initialState]]: initial direction, {{L}} (Left) or {{R}} (Right)
• [[leftTarget]]: target switch number or terminal depot identifier when set to {{L}}
• [[rightTarget]]: target switch number or terminal depot identifier when set to {{R}}
data.outputDescription: <<[[T]] lines>>: The name of the terminal depot reached by each train in dispatch order.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

An automated rail yard contains N switches, numbered 1 to N. Each switch is initially set to L (Left) or R (Right) and has a target for each direction. A target is either another switch, or a terminal depot with an identifier that is not a switch number.

• All trains are dispatched sequentially.
• Each train starts at switch 1.
• When a train enters a switch, it follows the target indicated by the switch's current direction, then the switch toggles to the opposite direction.
• The new direction applies to the subsequent train that enters the switch.
• A train stops when it reaches a terminal depot.

Given the initial switch states and track layout, determine the terminal depot reached by each train.
Input
Line 1: An integer N representing the number of switches.
Line 2: An integer T representing the number of trains to dispatch.
Next N lines: Space-separated values for a switch:
• id: switch number
• initialState: initial direction, L (Left) or R (Right)
• leftTarget: target switch number or terminal depot identifier when set to L
• rightTarget: target switch number or terminal depot identifier when set to R
Output
T lines: The name of the terminal depot reached by each train in dispatch order.
Constraints
1 ≤ N ≤ 10
1 ≤ T ≤ 10
1 ≤ id ≤ N
1 ≤ length of leftTarget, length of rightTarget ≤ 9
The track network contains no loops, meaning that a train never visits the same switch more than once.
Every train eventually reaches a terminal depot.
Example
Input
3
3
1 L 2 3
2 L E1 E2
3 L E3 E4
Output
E1
E3
E2
